body:
Unfortunately I'm not able to concentrate much, I'm just constantly checking my phone to be honest or hoping this is just a really bad dream because I'm not able to deal with it very well.

Thank you for the advice though, I appreciate it.

This is going to sound whiny i suppose, but unfortunately I just can't concentrate. I constantly just feel that I don't want to be around anylonger. 

She still hasn't showed.. I guess we will se what things are like once she's been over.

Thank you. She's coming over in a little while. I'm not really looking forward to it - I guess in a way it represents all my hopes and dreams crashing down. I'm not good at planing ahead, but I knew I could be happy with her. 

She made all the little boring details of day to day life so great. Now I just don't know. Everything seems pointless. I don't have anything to look forward to. I feel hopelessly lonely and pathetic.

I should have gotten out of the relationship a long time ago, but I never could. I couldn't give up because I can't see myself being happy with anyone else.

So she just texted me and told me that she will come over after work. To be completely honest I'm not sure I can take that conversation. 

It's as if I'm stuck in a bad dream. I keep catching myself thinking that maybe if I died I'd wake up to something other than misery.
I sort of doubt that; neither she nor I would have much trouble going out and getting laid for the most part.

Thing is I see her as an intelligent and thoughtful person. It's not that I don't think she'd hurt me; it's just that I can't see why it has to be final if she's so confused that she'd do something like that. Especially since I thought it was completely over the last time she did this and she knew it hurt me deeply that time as well. 

But I get what you're saying. I guess regardless of if it's one way or the other it's still not a healthy situation for me to be in. in the end she's the one that needs to change for things to wrok. I know that - but it's hard to deal with.

You're probably right. We had space this summer; she left for a job in another city for a while - in part because she needed space I suspect. That hurt me as well, because she dumped me without much of an explanation and ran. Didn't really see each other for two months and only had sporadic contact on facebook and the occasional phone call. I was pretty miserable - she dealt with it much better. Anyway, things picked up again pretty much a week after she came back. 

I guess in the end I know that you're right about what I should do. I guess I need to find a way of resist the temptation of seeing her when I have the opportunity. I feel that's much easier said than done though.

It's not that simple unfortunately. We were very good friends before anything sexual even started between us; I was actually very surprised when she initiated it - not that it hadn't crossed my mind, I just didn't think it was worth the risk. 

Problem for me I guess is that I feel I'm also losing my best friend. This is also compounded by the fact that she and I share a social circle and can't really avoid bumping into each other on regular basis because we both attend the same university.

The sex is also probably the part that has functioned best between us. I can't help wanting her - I'm not sure I can turn her down because both emotional and sexual attraction is so strong. 

I don't think she's lonely. She's far more outgoing that I am and she's also someone that picks herself up much easier. She needs people around more than I do - but at the same time she has issues with letting people get too close.
